note: Fits the physical and motivational half of the ICP cleanly and misses the commercial half. He is unambiguously not deconditioned — a former cross-country runner who plays competitive table tennis, volleyball and basketball — and his ask is textbook good-to-great: athleticism, posture, shoulder strength, 'being the best self', not rescue. Health is a neglected edge rather than a crisis, with no condition, injury or medication disclosed anywhere in this file. Where he falls outside is the part of the stated ICP that does the qualifying work. Occupation is never established at any point in the call — not asked, not volunteered — so 'they own their own business, or they're a physician, something along those lines' cannot be met on the evidence, and nothing in his language suggests it. On income the evidence points the wrong way: he asked for a payment plan twice, said he had overspent over the previous two or three months and needed to hold back, and was checking a credit card limit at the moment of purchase before switching cards to accommodate it. That is not 'they make good money' as the ICP means it. He closed at full price anyway, which makes this the second case in the corpus of a full-price close from outside the income criterion — after Robyn Stillwater — and it strengthens the standing observation in icp.json that 'the buying population is wider than the stated ICP'. The sharper version of that finding is visible here: income screening is not filtering these prospects out, it is just going unasked, and this prospect financed the purchase on credit rather than out of surplus. Also worth recording for the rollup that the profile the corpus keeps producing for this rep is younger and more discretionary-income-constrained than the executive-or-physician picture the ICP describes.
